distinguishing_features: Injection of a thermally conductive, gas-impermeable micro-encapsulant into interface voids at HV cable joints
Thermal expansion of the encapsulant generates hydrostatic pressure to collapse voids during hot cycles
Maintains a solid-liquid interface with high dielectric strength to prevent partial discharge
Utilizes temperature-dependent mechanical action of a phase-changing material to actively suppress void formation
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Preventing partial discharge in high-voltage cable joints caused by thermal cycling-induced void expansion at dielectric interfaces
parsed.viable_reason: The proposed material properties and pressures are within achievable ranges for polymer composites and XLPE insulation limits.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The use of a thermally expanding micro-encapsulant to actively compress voids during operation is not a routine adaptation of prior monitoring or sealing techniques.
